title: Console backend: release notes feed + per-model change history endpoints (filters, pagination, RBAC)
creator: Jada Williams
project: Model metadata schema v1 + changelog generator
body:
## Context
We need Console backend APIs to power the new customer-facing release notes surfaces:
- Console-wide Release notes feed
- Model details \"History\" tab (per-model)
- Rollouts UI \"What’s changing?\" panel (pulls release note entry for candidate version)

This ticket implements the Console backend endpoints and server-side filtering/pagination/RBAC required by the UX spec.

Primary UX reference:
- Confluence: `Console UX Spec: Model Change History & Release Notes (Rollouts/A-B)` (Kenji Nakamura, last updated 2025-10-18)
  - Expected filters: time range, deployment mode, region, category, model selector; toggle \"Affected my workspace\"
  - RBAC: customer roles see only public release notes; internal roles can optionally view internal details (server-enforced)

## Problem
Today model/version change info is fragmented. Even after we generate changelog entries, Console needs a stable API contract that:
- supports fast list views and filtering
- supports stable pagination (no dupes/missing entries when new notes land)
- enforces strict public vs internal separation (defense-in-depth)
- supports the workspace-impact filter without exposing raw usage telemetry

## Scope
### In scope (v1)
1) Release notes list endpoint for global feed
2) Per-model change history endpoint (same underlying data, with model_id pinned)
3) Filtering: time range, category, deployment mode(s), region(s), model_id(s)
4) Pagination: cursor-based with deterministic ordering
5) RBAC and redaction rules:
   - Customer roles: only public rendering
   - Internal roles: ability to request \"include_internal\" but gated and audited
6) Minimal rollout-panel support: fetch release note entry for a specific model+version candidate (API design below)
7) Telemetry + basic metrics for p95 latency and request volume

### Out of scope (this ticket)
- Console UI work (DES-611 + ENG-????)
- Docs site generation
- Notification subscriptions (email/webhooks)
- Full-text search (UX spec calls out as optional v1.1)

## Proposed API (Console backend → Console UI)
Note: naming below is implementation-friendly; final route names should align with Console API conventions.

### 1) List release notes (global feed)
`GET /console/v1/release-notes`

Query params:
- `time_start` (RFC3339, optional)
- `time_end` (RFC3339, optional)
- `category` (optional; one of: breaking, security, performance, quality, bugfix, deprecation)
- `severity` (optional; low|medium|high)
- `deployment_modes` (optional, repeatable: hosted|dedicated|private)
- `regions` (optional, repeatable)
- `model_ids` (optional, repeatable)
- `affected_workspace` (optional bool; default true for this endpoint per UX spec)
- `include_internal` (optional bool; default false; ignored/forced false for customer roles)

Pagination:
- `limit` (default 25, max 100)
- `cursor` (opaque)

Sorting:
- Default: `effective_at desc, id desc`
  - `effective_at` defined as the first time the entry becomes effective in any scope; UI will show more granular \"Effective in\" status using per-scope fields.

Response (conceptual fields; exact JSON shape tracked in ENG-9823 contract):
- `items[]`: release note entry cards
- `next_cursor`
- `applied_filters` (server echo, optional)

### 2) Per-model change history
`GET /console/v1/models/{model_id}/change-history`

Same filters/pagination as above, but `model_id` is required and implicitly applied.

### 3) Rollouts panel helper (candidate lookup)
Option A (preferred): reuse list endpoint with a strict filter
`GET /console/v1/release-notes?model_ids=...&to_version=...&limit=1`

Option B: direct lookup by version pointer (if generator guarantees 1:1 mapping)
`GET /console/v1/models/{model_id}/versions/{version}/release-note`

Decision: start with Option A to avoid coupling Console to generator assumptions; add Option B later if performance/clarity requires.

## RBAC + redaction (must-have)
RBAC rules per UX spec:
- Customer roles (Viewer/Developer/Workspace Admin):
  - Never receive internal-only fields
  - Never receive raw event IDs, actor identity, internal links, audit log links
- Internal roles (Support/Release Eng/Security/Super Admin):
  - Default response still public rendering
  - `include_internal=true` reveals internal sections ONLY for permitted roles

Implementation requirements:
- Server-side redaction is mandatory; client-side hiding is not sufficient.
- `include_internal=true` must be denied for customer roles even if they set it.
- Add an explicit allowlist of roles for internal fields; do not rely on \"isEmployee\" boolean.
- Ensure we do not leak internal content via:
  - error messages (e.g., validation failures that echo internal text)
  - partial responses (streaming/trace logs)
  - cached responses shared across roles (cache key must include permission tier)

Tie-in to ENG-9825:
- This ticket consumes the shared redaction/visibility library (or middleware) defined there.
- If ENG-9825 slips, we must still enforce a hard block: internal fields simply not fetched/returned.

## Workspace-impact filtering (\"affected_workspace\")
Definition from UX spec (summary): entry is included if its effective scope intersects workspace entitlements and models/versions actively used by the workspace.

Proposed v1 algorithm (pragmatic; matches spec intent without overfitting):
1) Compute eligible scope for workspace:
   - allowed deployment modes
   - enabled regions
2) Compute \"used models\" set:
   - pinned versions configured in workspace settings (if present)
   - active dedicated pool bindings (if dedicated)
   - private installed bundle version (if connected; if offline, treat as unknown and do entitlements-only)
   - hosted usage telemetry: last-30-days boolean \"model used\" (do NOT return counts)
3) Filter entries:
   - entry.effective_scope intersects eligible scope AND
   - (entry.model_id in used_models) OR (entry is category=deprecation affecting any entitled model)

Notes:
- Telemetry source must be optional. If unavailable, we fallback to entitlements-only and set a response hint flag (string field) for UI to show a small disclaimer (UX spec implies this).
- Must be careful for multi-model entries (if generator ever emits them). v1 assumes entries are per model; if not, we split server-side or exclude until generator enforces single-model.

## Pagination details
Cursor should encode:
- last_seen_effective_at
- last_seen_id
- plus the normalized filter set (or hash) to prevent cursor reuse across different queries

We should guarantee:
- stable ordering
- no duplicates across pages
- consistent results even if new items are added between requests (standard cursor semantics)

## Observability / metrics
Add basic metrics:
- request count by endpoint + status
- p50/p95 latency
- redaction_denied count (attempts to request include_internal without perms)
- affected_workspace_fallback_without_telemetry count

Add structured logs (no internal text in customer-request logs).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `GET /console/v1/release-notes` supports filters: time range, category, deployment_modes, regions, model_ids, affected_workspace
- [ ] `GET /console/v1/models/{model_id}/change-history` supports same filters and returns only that model
- [ ] Cursor pagination implemented with deterministic ordering and max limit enforcement
- [ ] Customer roles never receive internal-only fields even if `include_internal=true`
- [ ] Internal roles can request internal details and see expanded content (gated)
- [ ] Cache keys/response caching (if any) are permission-aware (no cross-role leakage)
- [ ] Unit tests for RBAC redaction and pagination edge cases
- [ ] Contract test against changelog generator service (ENG-9823) covering at least: public entry, internal entry, mixed-scope entry, reverted/rollback status
- [ ] Basic metrics/logging landed and dashboard hook added (at least a Datadog/Sumo query documented)

## Risks / edge cases
- \"Effective in\" computations: generator provides per-scope rollout status; if missing, we may need to approximate. Avoid inventing ETAs.
- Private offline: data availability is different; endpoint should degrade gracefully and not 500.
- Performance: filtered queries could become expensive if we compute workspace-impact in-line. Consider precomputing a workspace-model usage index or delegating scope evaluation to changelog service.
- Data leakage: any internal note leak is a security incident; regression tests are mandatory.

## Implementation notes
- Prefer to proxy through a single internal service API (changelog generator) rather than querying registry + events separately.
- Normalize filters in a shared helper so feed + model history behave identically.
- Keep the response payload aligned with the card component needs (avoid returning giant internal blobs by default).

## Links
- Confluence UX spec: `confluence://product-docs/design-specs/console-model-change-history-and-release-notes-ux-spec`
- Related tickets:
  - ENG-9823 (generator service internal API)
  - ENG-9825 (public vs internal fields redaction rules)
  - ENG-9828 (audit log events)
  - DES-611 (mocks)

## Rollout plan
- Stage behind feature flag: `console_release_notes_v1`
- Dogfood on internal workspaces first (Support + Release Eng)
- Then enable for 1–2 enterprise beta accounts (per PM-413), customer roles only
comments: 2025-10-10 — Chloe Martin: Please align endpoint naming with existing Console conventions (we’ve been using `/console/v1/...`). Also: pagination must be cursor-based; offset pagination caused dupes in the incidents feed.

2025-10-14 — Naomi Feldman: Security note: internal-only sections must be server-side stripped and not even serialized for customer requests. Also ensure cache keys include permission tier; we’ve had leaks in other services via shared CDN keys.

2025-10-18 — Kenji Nakamura: UX spec update: default on global feed is `affected my workspace = true`, but on model history default is `show all changes`. Please support both as a param; UI will set defaults per screen.

2025-10-22 — Felix Schneider: Draft contract implemented behind feature flag. Still waiting on finalized redaction library from ENG-9825; currently hard-forcing `include_internal=false` for all roles until we wire allowlist.
2025-10-24 — Jada Williams: For rollout panel, let’s reuse list endpoint w/ strict filters (Option A). We can add direct lookup later once we see generator invariants in production.

2025-10-29 — Marcus Lin: Reviewed RBAC approach. Requirement: log `include_internal` attempts denied (no PII) + add regression tests specifically for "internal body" fields. Also ensure errors don’t echo rejected fields.

2025-11-01 — Felix Schneider: Marking In Review. PR up with endpoints + cursor pagination + initial RBAC enforcement. Remaining: wire workspace-impact computation to usage index (currently entitlements-only fallback) and add one more test covering mixed region scope.
